n: In December 1830, Sidney Rigdon, a well-known preacher from Ohio converted by the Lamanite missionaries, came to meet Joseph. The Lord introduces himself as Alpha and Omega, constant and eternal.

f.w: one eternal round
the same today as yesterday, and forever

n: Jesus Christ was crucified for the world’s sins so believers can become God’s children and be one with him as he is one with the Father.

f.w: that we may be one

n: The Lord has seen Sidney’s works and heard his prayers, and has prepared him for greater work.
Like John the Baptist, Sidney unknowingly prepared the way — his Reformed Baptist preaching readied many in Ohio to accept the restored gospel.

f.w: even as John, to prepare the way before me

n: Sidney had baptized for repentance, but his converts did not receive the Holy Ghost, since he lacked that authority.

f.w: they received not the Holy Ghost

n: Now, with priesthood authority, he shall baptize and his converts will receive the Holy Ghost by the laying on of hands, as in the apostles’ day.

f.w: even as the apostles of old

n: A great work will happen among the Gentiles, and the world’s folly and evils will be exposed.
God’s arm is not shortened — his power is undiminished — and he will show miracles to believers.

f.w: mine arm is not shortened

n: Those who ask in faith will cast out devils, heal the sick, and restore sight, hearing, speech, and mobility.

f.w: they shall heal the sick

n: Great things will soon be shown to humankind.
Without faith, nothing will be shown except destruction on “Babylon,” the symbol of worldly wickedness.

f.w: the wine of the wrath of her fornication

n: Only those ready to receive the fulness of the gospel truly do good.
God calls the weak, unlearned, and despised to “thresh the nations” — to separate the righteous from the wicked by the Spirit’s power.

f.w: the weak things of the world
thresh
f.g: to beat grain to separate kernels from husks.

n: Their arm will be God’s arm; he will shield and strengthen them and preserve them by his power.

f.w: buckler

n: The poor and meek will hear the gospel and look for Christ’s coming, which is near.

f.w: the poor and the meek shall have the gospel preached unto them

n: They will learn the parable of the fig tree: when leaves appear, summer is near — a sign of the closeness of Christ’s coming.

f.w: the parable of the fig tree

n: The Lord has sent the fulness of his gospel through Joseph and blessed him in his weakness.
Joseph holds keys to sealed mysteries from the foundation of the world to the Second Coming — if he stays faithful; otherwise another would replace him.

f.w: if not, another will I plant in his stead

n: Sidney should watch over Joseph so his faith does not fail; the Holy Ghost will guide him.

f.w: that his faith fail not

n: Sidney is to be Joseph’s scribe as the scriptures are revealed — the Joseph Smith Translation of the Bible, then underway.

f.w: thou shalt write for him
f.g: Sidney served as scribe for much of the Joseph Smith Translation (JST) of the Bible.

n: The elect will hear Christ’s voice, see him, stay spiritually awake, endure his coming, and be purified as he is.

f.w: purified, even as I am pure

n: Sidney should stay with Joseph and not forsake him.
When not writing, Joseph will prophesy, and Sidney will preach and use the prophets’ words to support Joseph’s teachings.

f.w: call on the holy prophets to prove his words
f.g: use scripture to confirm and support the new revelations.

n: Keep all covenants, and God will shake the heavens for their good; Satan will tremble and Zion will flourish.

f.w: Zion shall rejoice upon the hills

n: Israel will be saved in God’s time, led by the restored priesthood keys, never again to be confused.

f.w: Israel shall be saved in mine own due time

n: Lift up your hearts — your redemption is near.

f.w: your redemption draweth nigh

n: “Fear not, little flock”: the kingdom is theirs until Christ comes, and he comes quickly.

f.w: Fear not, little flock
